rationale: fsGroupChangePolicy=OnRootMismatch lets the kubelet skip its recursive ownership walk when the volume root already carries the pod fsGroup, the setgid bit and group rwx. The measured saving on the shared 128 GiB scientific cache is 153-305 s of cold start per Job. The skip is only sound when the producer that wrote the tree and the consumer that mounts it agree exactly on gid, on the mounted volume root, and on the producer owning every inode below it. A group mismatch does not merely forfeit the saving: once some pod's walk stamps the root with the consumer's group, a later pod skips while the producer keeps writing under its own group, and those files become unreadable. This register records the state of every fsGroup-bearing template; entries marked unverified have a producer whose identity could not be established from this repository.

authorities.sole-writer-in-pod: An init container in the same pod creates the tree under the contracted uid/gid before the runtime container starts, so the ownership the kubelet would enforce is already the ownership the writer produced.
authorities.sole-writer-job: A separate reviewed Job is the only writer of the claim and stages content under the same gid the consumer mounts with. No pair in this repository meets this today.
authorities.no-persistent-writable-tree: The pod mounts no writable persistent claim, so there is no tree for the walk to own and no state for a skip to miss.
authorities.hostpath-not-kubelet-managed: The pod's only non-ephemeral volume is a hostPath, whose mounter reports Managed: false, so the kubelet runs no ownership pass over it at all. There is no walk to remove and the policy would change nothing either way.
authorities.unverified-external-writer: The template already carries the policy but its producer is outside this repository, so producer/consumer agreement could not be verified here. Recorded, not endorsed.
authorities.uniform-consumer-group-on-dedicated-clai: Every pod that mounts the claim uses the same fsGroup and no other writer exists, so the first pod's walk adopts the tree and every later pod matches it. Sound only while the claim stays dedicated to consumers that share one group.

follow_up.item: align the acquisition, localization and serving filesystem identities
follow_up.why: acquisition writes gid 10001, the serving pod mounts fsGroup 1000, and the localization Job pins neither runAsUser nor runAsGroup. Until one gid spans the chain over one mounted root, no consumer may use OnRootMismatch, so the optimisation cannot be turned on for the serving path at all.

follow_up.item: sequenced one-time root adoption for many-writer shared caches
follow_up.why: A bootstrap Job rendered beside the stages that consume it proves nothing: nothing orders them, nothing stops the stages running first, and a matching root group and mode are also what an unrelated pod's default walk leaves behind. It needs a terminal content-addressed receipt carrying claim UID, filesystem group, job UID and applied-manifest digest, stage admission bound to that receipt, and exclusion of concurrent writers during first adoption.

rollout.reason: No producer/consumer pair in this repository currently satisfies the contract. The artifact acquisition Job writes as gid 10001 while the model runtime pod mounts with fsGroup 1000, so the root can never match both. The localization Job pins neither runAsUser nor runAsGroup, so the group its staged tree ends up owned by is undefined and it cannot be anyone's producer; the validator reports that rather than passing it. Aligning these identities is a deliberate change to running services and is not made here.
rollout.unblocks_when: producer and consumer are pinned to one gid over one mounted volume root, with the producer owning every inode below it, proven by assert_authority

invariants_enforced: A pod that sets fsGroup must pair it with fsGroupChangePolicy=OnRootMismatch or keep the Kubernetes default; a policy without an fsGroup is rejected as a no-op.
A persistent mount, read-only included, needs a producer that agrees on gid, on the mounted volume root, and on owning every inode below it. fsGroup ownership is applied per volume, not per mount.
A writable persistent mount needs a frozen writer identity: without a pinned runAsUser and runAsGroup the group its tree ends up owned by is undefined, so it can never be a producer.
An owned root is a whole mounted volume root. A descendant of one, or a mount reached through a subPath, is rejected because the kubelet compares only the mount.
A claim marked readOnly at the volume level beside a writable mount of the same claim is rejected; read-only intent belongs on the mount.
